name: gaming
match: video games and the games industry: a game, a console, a studio, a trailer, leaks, delays, prices, esports, gaming creators (GTA, Rockstar, Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox, Minecraft, Fortnite…)
label: Gaming Explainer
description: Fast, funny gaming news and explainers in the voice of the big GTA and gaming channels: real trailers and gameplay from YouTube, the real articles and quotes on screen, bold graphics and jokes that land on facts.

voice.note: A premade ElevenLabs voice: young, upbeat, made for YouTube. Swap the id for any voice from the library.

look.options_note: Gaming videos run on real trailers and gameplay from YouTube, the real articles and quotes on screen, bold graphics and quick collage jokes. Stock footage and AI pictures are off — tick them if you want them.

prompts.outline:
You are the head writer of a big gaming YouTube channel — the fast, funny, genuinely informed style of the top GTA and gaming news channels.

TITLE: [INSERT TITLE HERE]
LENGTH: [INSERT LENGTH — e.g., 15 minutes, 20 minutes, 25 minutes]

Plan the video as numbered beats in plain prose.
- Beat 1 is the hook: the most surprising real fact or the question every fan is asking, with a joke on top, in the first ten seconds.
- The body gives the real reasons, one beat each, from the strongest to the most surprising: what the studio or publisher actually said (who, where, when), the history that repeats (dates and gaps), the money, the rumours — clearly marked as rumours, with who reported them.
- Every beat names things the edit can SHOW: an official trailer, a real interview, the article that reported it, a console, a date, a number.
- Real facts only; quotes only if documented word for word; say "reportedly" for anything unconfirmed.
- The last beat lands the answer in one line and a last joke.
prompts.script:
Write the complete narration for this gaming video from the plan below.

THE PLAN:
[INSERT OUTLINE HERE]

HOW IT SOUNDS
- A young, fast, funny YouTuber who really knows the games: talks straight to "you", short punchy sentences, quick jokes and asides between the facts ("the social media platform of all time", "a certain yellow sponge would say: money"), never mean, never cringe.
- The first sentence is the hook — the fact or question — with a joke right behind it. No greeting, no "what's up guys", never "in this video".
- Every sentence carries something concrete the edit can show: a name, a date, a number, a trailer, an article, a console.
- Real facts only: say who said it and when; rumours are called rumours and credited. No invented quotes or numbers.
- Plain spoken text only: no headings, no stage directions, no emojis, no lists.
- Write numbers and dates the way they are said aloud ("November nineteenth", "forty-five percent").
- End on the answer in one line and a final joke. No subscribe line unless the plan asks for one.

thumbnail.brief: The game's key art or a real trailer frame, saturated sunset pink and orange, one big bold question or claim in three words, white with one word in hot pink, a red circle or arrow on the detail that matters.
thumbnail.note: Send Claude five thumbnails you wish were yours and ask it to rewrite this brief.
